## Appearance

Faith features golden-brown eyes and matching golden-brown curls. Her cheeks are distinctly crimson.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P6](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0006)_

## Personality

Faith is a beautiful, spirited woman with an original, inspiring, and inherently joyous nature that shuns disagreeable topics. Though her heedless, impulsive disposition and love for mischief frequently lead her into trouble, she possesses a proud side that refuses to play second fiddle to anyone. She harbors a firm resolve to never marry a minister and finds her imagination gripped by the fear of a ghost.

## History

Faith Meredith moved to [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) St. Mary from [Maywater](../codex/places.md#maywater), where she had been given a pet rooster named [Adam](../character/adam.md) as a chick. After arriving in the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen), she and her siblings befriended the [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) children in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) and helped house a runaway orphan named [Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md). Due to losing track of the days, Faith and her sister [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) accidentally performed their household chores on a Sunday, sparking a local scandal. Faith attempted to compensate for her mistake by addressing the church congregation, and she later rode pigs through the [Glen](../codex/places.md#glen) on a dare with [Walter Blythe](../character/walter-blythe.md). Upon learning that her father's position in the ministry was endangered by a lack of financial support, Faith confronted the eccentric [Norman Douglas](../character/norman-douglas.md) and persuaded him to attend church and contribute to her father's salary. When her pet rooster [Adam](../character/adam.md) was killed to feed a visiting minister, Faith expressed her anger by allowing the minister's coat-tails to catch fire, though she was later comforted by [Rosemary West](../character/rosemary-west.md). Following repeated public embarrassments, Faith joined her siblings in forming a self-disciplining [Good-Conduct Club](../codex/factions.md#good-conduct-club). After giving her good stockings to a needy girl, Faith attended church bare-legged to avoid wearing striped stockings, causing another scandal which she attempted to resolve by writing a letter of explanation to the local newspaper.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P5](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER IV. THE MANSE CHILDREN P37](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0037), [v5 CHAPTER IV. ## Quotes

> "Here, Una, you stir it while I set the table. If I leave it for a minute the horrid stuff will burn. It’s half past nine. We’ll be late for Sunday School."
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE P15](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0015)

> "I’d hate to think the Methodists were better at going to Sunday School on rainy Sundays than the Presbyterians. But there’s no preaching in their Church to-day, either, so likely their Sunday School is in the afternoon."
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE P20](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0020)

> "I like being myself. It’s more interesting. Jessie Drew is as good a housekeeper as her mother, but would you want to be as stupid as she is?"
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER X. THE MANSE GIRLS CLEAN HOUSE P23](../source/v05-c10.md#nw-v05-c10-p0023)

> "Just as soon as you get fond of a place you are torn up by the roots. I’ll never, never, never marry a minister, no matter how nice he is."
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER XV. MORE GOSSIP P37](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0037)

> "I love birds. Only—would Aunt Martha’s cat eat it? It’s so tragic to have your pets eaten. I don’t think I could endure it a second time."
>
> — Faith — [v5 CHAPTER XX. FAITH MAKES A FRIEND P34](../source/v05-c20.md#nw-v05-c20-p0034)
